title: Asymmetric batch misalignment telemetry notes
content:
Summary:

This note captures an investigation into repeated Nsight traces where one subset of SMs shows sustained low active warps during mixed-size microbatch workloads. The root cause appears related to asymmetric batching and CUDA-graph replay alignment: when we stitch larger requests onto microbatches that are slightly misaligned with our kernel batching window, several kernels become short-lived and leave SM slots idle for the subsequent kernel launch, reducing overall occupancy and increasing tail latency.

Why this matters:
- Higher cost per token: lower SM utilization translates directly into fewer tokens/sec on the same fleet.
- Tail latency spikes: idle periods between kernel handoffs increase 99th/99.9th percentile response times.
- Unpredictable replay variance: CUDA-graph capture/replay amplifies the misalignment (replayed graphs assume contiguous execution windows).

Environment and dataset used:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 80GB (nvlink enabled), CUDA 12.3, driver 535.xx
- Software: runtime branch batching-experiment-2027 (serving-runtime commit 0b9a5f), pytorch 2.2 + custom fused kernels
- Workload: mixed sequence lengths (32/128/512) with request mix 40/40/20; synthetic client that simulates arrival jitter (poisson lambda tuned to hit microbatch size 16 most of the time)
- Traces: Nsight Systems (syst) captures + Nsight Compute (ncu) for hot kernels; also collected timeline CSV from our in-house microbatch tracer

Capture commands used (examples):
- nsight-sys: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --sample=cpu --output=trace_misaligned_0803
- ncu: ncu --target-processes all --set full --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm__pipe_active.avg.pct,sm__sass_thread_inst_executed.avg
- internal tracer: ./microbatch_tracer --dump-timeline=timeline_0803.csv --include-kv-cache-events

Key observations from traces:
1) Handoff holes after short kernels: The decoder-head kernel for short sequences (32) finishes quickly and then we observe a 200-800us quiet window before the next large-kernel starts. During the quiet window we still have threads in the scheduler but no active warps recorded by achieved_occupancy metric.
2) CUDA-graph replay mismatch: When the replay path is used, graphs captured under a particular batch alignment assume contiguous kernel ordering. If an immediate preceding microbatch is shorter, the graph replays with an inserted delay (host-side scheduling delay), causing the device to miss coalesced launches that would have otherwise filled SMs.
3) L2 bank conflict amplification: Timeline overlays show that when the short-to-long transition happens, L2 read bursts from the long kernel overlap with residual writes from the earlier kernel's epilogue, producing higher L2 bank conflict counters and degrading effective memory throughput by ~18% in that phase.
4) Stream priority variance: We found that using default stream priorities increases handoff jitter: higher-priority streams preempt kernel submission order and occasionally cause kernel reordering during microburst periods.
5) Occupancy skew across SMs: Sampling shows a bimodal occupancy distribution — ~65% for half the SMs, ~22% for the other half — consistent across several captures when batch misalignment occurs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Misaligned microbatch sizes create short-lived kernels that leave launch windows unfilled, causing SM idle time; captured CUDA graphs cannot represent these transient windows, so replay exacerbates the issue.
- H2: Host-side queueing and our current kernel coalescer do not perform a tight-enough merge on adjacent microbatches when sequence lengths differ, producing separate kernel launches instead of one fused launch.
- H3: Stream priority handling combined with NVTX delimiting is causing launches to be sequenced suboptimally in the presence of small/large back-to-back requests.

Evidence for H1/H2:
- Timeline shows separate kernel launches with small gaps; patching the microbatch coalescer locally to force-fuse adjacent kernels (when combined warp count < threshold) reduced quiet windows and improved tokens/sec by ~12% in a short A/B run.
- NCU metrics for fused vs unfused runs: fused run improved achieved_occupancy from 41% -> 63% for the mixed workload.

Quick experiments tried and outcomes:
- Force-disable CUDA-graph replay in runtime: resolved misaligned replay variance but slightly increased average latency due to more host submissions.
- Coalesce adjacent microbatches more aggressively (local patch): improved throughput and smoothed occupancy but increased host-side scheduling CPU overhead by ~6%.
- Run with explicit stream priorities disabled (single priority): reduced reordering but didn't eliminate quiet windows.

Actionable next steps:
1) Instrumentation: add a lightweight tracer to mark kernel launch pairings and host submission timestamps (owner: Marco). Goal: quantify host-side delay distribution across 100k requests.
2) Runtime change: implement a heuristic in the microbatch coalescer to fuse launches when sequence-length variance between adjacent microbatches is below threshold and combined warps < N (owner: Asha).
3) CUDA-graph strategy: implement a fallback capture approach — record a short graph for the common-case aligned layout and a separate mini-graph for short-edge cases; select at replay time based on recent batch alignment stats (owner: Danielle).
4) Experiment: schedule an A/B test on one Dedicated cluster to compare tokens/sec and 99th latency with the fused coalescer vs baseline for two weeks (owner: infra SRE lead Omar). Add experiment to INF-1932.

Notes / open questions:
- How much host CPU overhead can we tolerate for more aggressive coalescing? Need cost model.
- Does this issue manifest on other GPU SKUs (H100, L40)? Preliminary quick run on H100 showed similar trend but smaller gaps (likely due to different kernel launch latency).
- Could a device-side kernel aggregator (persistent kernel) reduce host launches while keeping flexibility? Worth prototyping but larger engineering effort.

Attachments and links: see linked_artifacts. I also exported the Nsight CSVs to GDrive folder /traces/2027-08 and left sample timeline_0803.csv there.

Immediate todo (this week):
- Marco: push tracer PR (small, adds ~60 bytes of NVTX per launch)
- Asha: land coalescer heuristic behind feature-flag + smoke tests
- Danielle: prototype multi-graph replay selection logic in a branch and include capture heuristics

If useful I can paste the short ncu output and the microbatch tracer CSV into this doc in the next revision. For reviewers: please call out any additional metrics you want pulled from NCU or the timeline CSV (e.g., l2_throughput_line_rate, dram_utilization_pct).

End of note.
